speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All our economic policies, be they free trade agreements or foreign manpower policies, are about creating jobs for our people and helping Singaporeans achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many of you will remember: Mr Lee Kuan Yew took special care to make the road leading from Changi Airport to the city as attractive as possible to impress foreign investors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They see this tree-lined road and their first impression is that this is a well-run place, able to plan and implement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it is safe to invest here and create jobs here.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is the level of detail, the persistence and devotion, that carries on to this day – all to secure jobs and livelihoods for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have explained to Singaporeans many times, our approach and policies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have debated in this House too, including recently in July.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai has also filed a Motion on this matter.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had invited him to do so earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are prepared to fight any party that chooses to take a populist line and stirs racism and xenophobia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The pace of change in our economy has accelerated over the decades.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Think about what our economy was like in the early 1990s.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, PMETs made up just about 30% of our local workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It was rare to hear of PMETs being retrenched.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There was a higher chance of retrenchments amongst non-PMETs, but not so much amongst PMETs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Inevitably, we are seeing more retrenchments amongst them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And though the absolute number of layoffs is not many, even those who are in good jobs worry and wonder if they might be next.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The pandemic has also increased the economic churn and uncertainty and deepened these worries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is the same all around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In part, this is the result of the churn that happens in any vibrant economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In some sectors, firms will close and let go of people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other sectors, there will be growth and more promising jobs being created.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Technology is accelerating this churn due to the disruptions it causes across all sectors of the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In some places, the churn they are experiencing is coupled with structural difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, entire industries going down with no new jobs to replace, and places like these have started to turn inwards and become more protectionist.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But that is not a viable option for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a small island state with no natural resources and no hinterland, the only way we can survive and prosper is to stay open and connected.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And, indeed, we have thrived over the decades only because we are an open economy and a business hub.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Global businesses see value in locating their regional and global functions here.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Homegrown enterprises benefit, too, because they can expand easily to markets overseas and access opportunities everywhere around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, businesses choose Singapore because of our openness, our rule of law and our consistency in policies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will hire many Singaporeans because they know the quality of our people: their skills, their drive, their honesty.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And, indeed, the quality of the Singaporean workforce is one reason why they came here in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are not enough Singaporeans to fill all the jobs available.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Moreover, as international companies, they want to have a diverse workforce and to move their staff around their different offices to develop them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, here, in Singapore, they bring together the best team to oversee their regional and global operations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What is our response to these global businesses?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Do we want them in Singapore or not?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These companies can locate their functions in any other hub city, be it Hong Kong, New York or London.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we were to take a politically craven approach and impose many stringent conditions on their ability to operate here, we will lose out on many good investments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But many Singaporeans will also be deprived of good jobs and career opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is like cutting off one’s nose to spite one’s face.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our aim is to create good jobs and improve the lives of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Look at the data over the last decade.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Income growth at the lower end has kept pace with the median.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, household incomes have also risen across the board.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our employment rate has been amongst the highest in the world; our unemployment rate has been kept low.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Look at the PMET data – professionals, managers, executives, technicians.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is almost three times the increase in EP and S Pass holders over the same time period, which was about 110,000.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are substantial achievements which we can be proud of and which we should celebrate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the PSP wants to sweep these aside.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They downplay the jobs, opportunities and outcomes we have created, and play up the anxieties.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The PSP assumes that if we reduced the number of foreigners here, then all these jobs will automatically go to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai has a euphemism for it.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He called it in one of his earlier Facebook posts, “rebalancing”.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is quite clear what he means.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In one post, he said we can get rid of “tens of thousands”, I quote, "tens of thousands" of work pass holders and he thinks that Singaporeans can then fill these jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With so many companies having difficulties filling these vacancies, how would we find people with the relevant skillsets to take on the additional “tens of thousands” of jobs that Mr Leong thinks can be created by getting rid of the foreigners?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, if our policies were to become overly restrictive, companies will just find other places to operate in where they can be more competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We would lose all the jobs they brought here.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if we are not careful, decades of hard work to build up our business hub will be wasted.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economy will contract and go down in a tailspin.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will end up with far worse problems, and it is not the foreigners but Singaporeans who will, ultimately, pay the price.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For those who would like to see fewer foreign work pass holders, they may perhaps be feeling a sense of nostalgia about how things were like in the past.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us say we go back to the 1990s.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Back then, we were not as developed as a hub economy; so foreign PMETs accounted for just 10% of our PMET workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But remember, our overall standards of living were also much lower then.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Stagnate in the 1990s, while the rest of the world progresses around us?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Remember how Mr Lee Kuan Yew once said, “Never fear, 10 years from now, this will be a metropolis”.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What do Mr Leong Mun Wai and the PSP promise: “10 years from now, we will go back 30 years”?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The reality is that as a business hub, we cannot escape global competition, whether it comes from China or India or the developed countries or cities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But by combining and complementing local and foreign professionals, we are able to attract more investments, including from cutting-edge companies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, we can grow the pie, create many more good jobs and career choices for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And, in fact, companies are actively hiring locals into PMET jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most of our local graduates are snapped up as soon as they enter the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the past decade, nine in 10 were employed within six months after graduation, with starting salaries rising steadily.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And our resident PMET unemployment rate remains low.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Twenty years ago, few Singaporeans wanted to study computer science.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It was one of the least popular courses in our Universities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, the IT sector has grown manifold and there is huge demand for tech professionals in every sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Computer science is now an extremely popular course and its graduates are in huge demand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The median starting salary of a computer science University fresh graduate is around $4,000 to $5,000 a month.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year, around 7,600 local students enrolled in ICT courses in our Universities, Polytechnics and ITEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) are producing as many ICT graduates as they can.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But you can see from the data that relying on the local pipeline alone will not be enough.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also need to balance the needs of other sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because if we increase the intake of young people in ICT too sharply, we will end up with fewer people in other areas like nursing or physiotherapy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, the complaint will not be about foreigners in IT but foreigners in our hospitals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not just the number of jobs that has grown.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Career choices have also expanded as we become more vibrant as a hub economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More than 20 years ago, the sector was smaller and the jobs available were more domestically focused than today.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most of the jobs then were in our three local retail banks: DBS, OCBC and UOB.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, the financial services sector has grown significantly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our local banks now have a good overseas footprint.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, we have anchored major international banks like the Asia Pacific operations of Citi and the global operations of Standard Chartered, as well as a wider variety of other players, including private banks, asset managers, specialist and reinsurance firms, fintech companies and more.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They serve not only the domestic market, but also the larger regional and global markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Just in recent months, we have seen Singaporeans being appointed new leadership positions in various international firms including Deutsche Bank and HSBC, as they expand their operations here.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we anchor more businesses here and as they expand their footprint, there will be more opportunities for Singaporeans as well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the data and evidence are clear: our economic policies have helped to raise living standards across the board, and to create many good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our children – fresh graduates from our IHLs, Polys and ITEs – are benefiting.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are doing the jobs of the future, not the past, which would have disappeared in any event if we had stood still in the 1990s.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They reflect the lived experiences of the vast majority of Singaporeans, whose lives have improved as a result of our policies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we know that globalisation is not an unmitigated good.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Being a hub economy brings many benefits to Singapore and Singaporeans but it also comes with its share of costs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The rapid pace of change and the “creative destruction” that takes place in any vibrant economy mean that there will be people displaced from their jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the issue is not about foreigners working here.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even if we got rid of “tens of thousands” of foreigners, locals will continue to be displaced because of technology, because of innovation, because of the changing nature of work over time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the rise of remote work, people can work from anywhere in the world and they need not be all in the same place.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the face of these painful dislocations, it is easy for politicians to blame someone for them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: People do not lose jobs because of technology or innovations, they say, but it is because of the foreigners in our midst; they are the reason you have been displaced.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if they can mobilise existing racial prejudices against particular foreign nationalities here, better still.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we see nationalist and protectionist sentiments gaining ground everywhere around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why populist and anti-immigrant parties – even neo-Nazis and fascists – do well in many European countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Far easier to point fingers, make one nationality or another the scapegoat and blame them for all our troubles, rather than work on reskilling our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I emphasise again: there are downsides to an open economy and these must be attended to.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if we want an economy where nobody will ever be displaced, then we will stagnate and atrophy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the right approach is not to impede progress by holding on to every job even as they become obsolete, but to work hard to protect every worker and help those who are displaced.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this way, we grow the economic pie for everyone, and ensure that the cost of globalisation and openness does not fall unfairly on the displaced workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is, indeed, the approach we, the PAP and NTUC, have taken.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On an overall basis, the pluses of what we have been able to achieve far outweigh the negatives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we have taken and will continue to take proactive steps to deal with the downsides.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we are continually updating our manpower policies and rules to ensure that the flow of work pass holders is managed and they are of the right calibre.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hence, we review and update the criteria for work pass holders over time and I will elaborate on this later in my speech.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we uphold fair employment practices and take a strong stance against discrimination at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know that some Singaporeans have experienced this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Their foreign colleagues may not be up to scratch.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They may have been unfairly passed over for a promotion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They may have been victims of discriminatory hiring practices.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Prime Minister spoke frankly about these issues at the National Day Rally (NDR).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise the pain and the frustration of those who feel unfairly treated by a foreign boss or a foreign colleague.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When our agencies pick up problematic indicators in a firm, we place the firm on the watchlist for closer scrutiny and our agencies step in to intervene, quietly but effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had deliberated over this for some time and had hesitated to do this in the past.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To be fair, the majority of companies do behave responsibly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we know that unfair practices occur from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will spare no effort in investigating every case thoroughly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Where companies are found wanting, there will be consequences.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, we do everything we can to help those who are displaced.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To every person who loses his job, the unemployment rate is 100%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Losing one's job is disorienting and disabling; there are no two ways about it.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take the example of Mr Edwin Chee, who was retrenched in May 2019 as an engineer in a manufacturing firm.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Edwin took the plunge and made a career switch to the rapidly growing medical technology industry.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through the programme, Edwin learnt the ins-and-outs of the sector, picked up new skills and successfully pivoted into his new role as a senior engineer.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, Edwin has settled into his new role and enjoys better prospects in this rapidly growing industry.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are doing everything we can to help displaced workers get back into jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to minimise their time out of a job, help them find good job matches that build on their wealth of skills and experience, and give them an injection of skills, if needed, for the new job.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are the major undertakings under the National Jobs Council chaired by Senior Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some of our current schemes are temporary incentives for jobs which will be tapered down as the economy recovers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we are not going back to the pre-COVID-19 status quo ante.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOF is working through these details carefully to make sure that the changes we make are financially sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I promise all Singaporeans, especially those who are displaced: you will never be alone.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to invest in your capabilities and skills; help you stay competitive; and walk this journey with you through the rest of your careers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai's Motion states that the Government's "foreign talent policy" is the cause of job anxieties.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But he is barking up the wrong tree because the issue is not about local talent versus foreign talent.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not a zero-sum competition, as I have explained.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do this by first nurturing and growing our own talent, because Singaporeans will always be our priority and at the centre of everything we do.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We start from young through significant investments in preschool and education to help every child achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also broadening our conception of merit and giving people opportunities to advance and excel across different domains and at multiple stages of their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we continue to bring in manpower and skills from around the world to complement our own people, to give us that extra boost so we can continue to thrive amidst intense global competition.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do this across every level of the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the lower end of the income spectrum, we bring in Work Permit holders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The numbers are quite large, but we need them in areas like construction and marine.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we control the flow with quotas and levies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For the middle-income tier, we have Singaporeans doing the jobs, but there are not enough of them and we need to top-up with S Pass holders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We control the flow with quotas and levies, but we also impose minimum qualifying salaries to make sure they have the right skill sets and are in areas where we need them most.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the higher level, we bring in professionals with the abilities and skills to contribute at the upper end of the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We need the right instrument to manage the flow of these foreign professionals and ensure they are of the right calibre.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is best achieved not through levies and quotas, but through the salary cut-offs, because how much the employer is prepared to pay is a practical indicator of quality.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to ensure that the qualifying salaries, for both S Passes and EPs, keep pace with our local wages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also studying how to further improve this framework to have a finer-grained feel for the people we bring in and ensure we get the right talent for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we constantly adjust the balance in our workforce and bring together the best talent for Team Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Based on this framework, we allow companies to bring in the workers they need at different levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The PSP has raised questions in Parliament on the nationality breakdown of the EPs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But from a competition and jobs perspective, where the EPs come from should not matter.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What is more important are the policy parameters I have just outlined, which determine the overall flow and the quality of the work pass holders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, if there are questions about this balance, we can discuss and debate the specific settings of our policies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But let us not turn this into an issue about CECA and Indian professionals, which are not relevant, unless the PSP intends to persist with its negative campaign to stir up racial unhappiness.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In short, Singapore will remain open and welcoming.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But those who do business here must also recognise the value of our workforce and abide by our rules.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to ensure that the companies we attract and root in Singapore are those who are committed to nurturing and growing our Singaporean Core.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singaporeans must be big-hearted and accepting of those who are different from us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Non-Singaporeans must respect our norms and way of life and make the effort to fit in.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we should not be starting this debate from zero.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: During the debate, Mr Leong Mun Wai acknowledged some of the points and he said, and I quote, that the PSP "fully supports FTAs" and is "in favour of having foreign talents or foreigners to come in to complement us".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, with that as the starting point, I look forward to hearing Mr Leong Mun Wai's further elaboration on the PSP's position today.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those were the two questions raised by Mr Ong Ye Kung then.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai had not given this House a clear answer to these two questions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The PSP has had two months to think about their answers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I hope that when Mr Leong Mun Wai rises next, he will speak clearly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The strong racist and xenophobic undertones in the PSP's campaign against CECA have not gone unnoticed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this is what he wrote and I quote, "due to such PSP campaign and what is falsely reported in social media, there is every possibility that Singaporeans who are shortlisting candidates may not shortlist me for interviews thinking that I am an India Indian.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I decided to indicate on the header of my resume on each page 'Singapore Citizen', but does this help?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I don’t think so… I seek your assistance that our Government put a stop to the PSP campaign which is truly racist and is hurting Singapore Indians and we are splitting Singaporeans along racist lines.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are little hairline cracks that if left unchecked will result in bigger issues in years to come." So, I appeal to the PSP, its two representatives here and its leadership outside the House.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you are truly concerned about the well-being of our fellow Singaporeans and the future of this country, please have a care about how you go about dealing with these issues.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Please reflect on how your rhetoric can deepen fault lines, not just between locals and foreigners, but even between Singaporeans of different races.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Please refrain from exploiting Singaporeans' anxieties for your own political gain.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope that when Mr Leong Mun Wai rises to speak later, he will share with us PSP's approach to deal with this important issue of jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have set out comprehensively the Government's strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We ensure every Singaporean has a place in our society and a share in our nation's progress.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We keep Singapore and Singaporeans together, not fractured.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope Mr Leong Mun Wai will give us a satisfactory answer later with concrete policy alternatives, and not resort to anti-foreigner rhetoric to stir anger and fear or disaffection against the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are no silver bullets or instant solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It would have been easy for us to make cosmetic changes for symbolic effect or political gestures but that is not the way we operate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our approach is to deal squarely with the difficult issues, to be upfront with Singaporeans about our challenges and trade-offs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We discuss with stakeholders, especially our tripartite partners.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We forge consensus on the way forward to bring about solutions that are durable, effective and sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Working together in this way, we have overcome crisis after crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: During bad times, we do not quarrel and fight over a shrinking pie.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we rally as a team to solve our problems and grow the pie for all to benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us continue to work together to build a better Singapore for ourselves, our children and our children's children.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In accordance with the decision of this House to take this Motion together with the next Motion standing in the name of Mr Leong Mun Wai, I will now call Mr Leong to move his Motion and make his opening speech before allowing Members to debate on both Motions.
